Rashi on Gittin 23b:10:1.hebrew: חמותה ובת חמותה כו' - בכולהו מפרש ביבמות דסניין לה ומכוונת לקלקלה, ואין נאמנות להעידה שמת בעלה:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:10:1.english: Her mother-in-law, and her mother-in-law's daughter, etc. - Regarding all of them, [the Gemara] explains in Yevamot that they hate her and intend to ruin her, and [therefore] they are not deemed credible to testify for her that her husband died:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:10:2.hebrew: יבמתה - אשת אחי בעלה שונאה אותה, ויראה ממנה שמא ימות אחד משני בעליהן בלא בנים, ויהו צרות זו לזו:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:10:2.english: Her yevamah - Her husband's brother's wife hates her, and is afraid of her lest one of their two husbands die without children and they become rival wives to one another:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:11:1.english: And what is [the difference] between a bill of divorce and death - [meaning] that regarding death they are not believed, whereas regarding a bill of divorce they are believed:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:12:1.english: In the Land [of Israel] - for she does not need to say, "In my presence it was written":

Rashi on Gittin 23b:14:1.english: Where if [the] husband comes [and] contests - and says, "I did not write it":

Rashi on Gittin 23b:14:2.hebrew: משגחינן ביה - שהרי לא נתקיים בבית דין, ואיכא למימר שזו מתכוונת לכך שתתקלקל:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:14:2.english: We pay attention to him - for [the bill of divorce] was not certified in court, and it can be said that this [woman] intends thereby that [the other woman] will come to ruin:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:14:3.hebrew: בחוצה לארץ - שהצריכוה לומר "בפני נכתב", וזהו קיומו, ותו לא חיישינן לערעור, ואי מערער לא מהימן:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:14:3.english: Outside of the Land [of Israel] - where they required her to say, "It was written in my presence," and this is its validation, and we are no longer concerned about a challenge, and if he challenges [it], he is not believed.

Rashi on Gittin 23b:1:1.hebrew: מכלל דעבד כשר - וכי היכי דכשר להבאה להיות שליח להתגרש, כך כשר לקבלה להיות שליח להתגרש, שאין חילוק טעם ביניהם:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:1:1.english: By inference, a slave is fit - And just as he is fit for bringing [a bill of divorce] to be an agent for [a woman] to be divorced, so too is he fit for receiving [it] to be an agent for [her] to be divorced, for there is no difference in reasoning between them:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:2:1.hebrew: הא במילתא דאיתיה - כגון תרומה, שאסור לעבד לאכול טבל, ואם יש לו טבל שניתן לו ע"מ שאין לרבו רשות בו, מפריש תרומה הימנו ותרומתו תרומה, דעבד כאשה בכל מצות; ותימא נמי דכשר להיות שליח לתרום:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:2:1.english: But in a matter that he is [included] in - For example, terumah, since a slave is forbidden to eat tevel [untithed produce], and if he has tevel that was given to him on condition that his master has no authority over it, he separates terumah from it and his terumah is [valid] terumah, for a slave is like a woman with respect to all mitzvot; and would you also say that he is fit to be an agent to separate terumah?

Rashi on Gittin 23b:3:1.hebrew: שתרמו את שלהן תרומתן תרומה - ואסורה לזרים, דסבר אין קנין לעובד כוכבים בארץ ישראל להפקיע מקדושת מעשר, והקדש העובד כוכבים הקדש, כדילפי' (חולין דף יג:) מאיש איש, לרבות את העובדי כוכבי' שנודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:3:1.english: That separated [terumah] from their own [produce], their terumah is [valid] terumah - and it is forbidden to non-priests, for [the Tanna] holds that an idolater has no [power of] acquisition in the Land of Israel to exempt [its produce] from the sanctity of tithes, and what an idolater consecrates is [validly] consecrated, as we derive (Chullin 13b) from [the phrase] "ish ish" [any man], to include idolaters, that they may vow vows and freewill-offerings like a Jew:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:3:2.hebrew: אפילו ברשותו - של ישראל שעשאו שליח, אין תרומתו תרומה:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:3:2.english: Even with his permission - [that] of the Jew who appointed him [as an] agent, his teruma is not teruma:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:4:1.english: What is the reason - [that it] is not terumah?

Rashi on Gittin 23b:4:2.hebrew: לאו משום - דשליחות דתרומה, דכתיב "כן תרימו גם אתם", ודרשינן: מדמצי למכתב "אתם" וכתב "גם אתם", לרבות שלוחכם; ואיתקש שליח לשולחו בהאי קרא, למימר דמה אתם בני ישראל אף שלוחכם ישראל, ומהאי מיעוטא איכא למעוטי נמי לעבד שתרם את של ישראל ברשות:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:4:2.english: Is it not because - [the law of] agency for terumah [is derived from that] which is written: "Thus you also shall set apart [a gift unto the Lord]" (Numbers 18:28), and we expound: since [Scripture] could have written "you" and [instead] wrote "you also," [it comes] to include your agent; and an agent is compared to the one who sends him in this verse, to say that just as you are Israelites, so too your agent [must be] an Israelite, and from this exclusion one can also exclude a slave who separated terumah from [the produce] of an Israelite with permission:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:5:1.english: No; just as you [are] members of the covenant - [Meaning, those who are] circumcised and have entered into the covenant of mitzvot:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:5:2.hebrew: אף שלוחכם בני ברית - לאפוקי עובד כוכבים, אבל עבד בן ברית הוא, דכתיב (דברים כט) "מחוטב עציך וגו'":
Rashi on Gittin 23b:5:2.english: So too, your agents are members of the covenant - [This comes] to exclude a gentile, whereas a [Canaanite] slave is a member of the covenant, as it is written (Deuteronomy 29[:10]): "from the hewer of your wood, etc.":

Rashi on Gittin 23b:6:1.hebrew: ואף ע"פ ששנינו - בברייתא במס' תמורה: האומר לשפחתו "הרי את שפחה וולדך בן חורין", אם היתה עוברה זכתה לו — לעובר, בקבלת גט זה להיות משוחרר:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:6:1.english: And although we learned - in a baraita in Tractate Temurah: [Regarding] one who says to his maidservant, "Behold you are a maidservant, and your child is a freeman," if she was pregnant, she has acquired [freedom] for him — [meaning] for the fetus, through receiving this bill [of manumission], to become emancipated:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:1.hebrew: מאי אם היתה עוברה - מה ענין שחרור אצל גט אשה, דקאמר "אע"פ ששנינו"? הא ודאי בתורת שחרור איתיה:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:1.english: What [is the meaning of] "If she was pregnant" - What does manumission have to do with a woman's bill of divorce, that [Rabbi Yochanan] said, "Even though we learned..."? For surely [a slave] is [included] in the law of manumission:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:2.hebrew: ר' יוחנן תרתי אמר - חדא: הא דגט אשה, ועוד אחריתי, ואמילתא אחריתי קאמר "אע"פ", והיינו מילתא אחריתי: נראין דברים שהעבד מקבל גט שחרור לחבירו:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:2.english: Rabbi Yochanan said two [statements] - One [is] this [ruling] regarding a woman's bill of divorce, and [there is] another [statement] as well, and it is regarding [that] other statement that he said "even though [we learned: if she was pregnant, she acquired freedom for him]," and this is the other statement: It appears that a slave can receive a bill of manumission for his fellow [slave]:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:3.hebrew: מיד רבו של חבירו - שאין רבו שלו, דכיון דעבד איתיה בתורת שחרור, שליח נמי מצי מיהוי:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:3.english: From the hand of his fellow's master - who is not his [own] master; for since a slave is subject to [the laws of] manumission, he can also become an agent [for this]:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:4.hebrew: אבל לא מיד רבו שלו - אם שניהם של איש אחד, דיד עבד כיד רבו דמי, וכשמסרו גט בידו לא יצא גט מרשותו; ואע"ג דעבד מקבל גט לעצמו, התם הוא דגיטו וידו באים כאחד, דשיחרורא דידיה הוא, אבל לאחרינא לא:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:7:4.english: But not from the hand of his own master - If both [slaves] belong to one person, since a slave's hand is like his master's hand, when [the master] places the bill [of manumission] into his hand, the bill has not left [the master's] possession. And even though a slave can receive a bill [of manumission] for himself, there it is because his bill [of manumission] and his hand come simultaneously, as it is his own emancipation; but for another [slave], [he can]not:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:8:1.hebrew: ואם לחשך אדם - באזנך להקשות ולומר: הרי שנויה היא שאף מיד רבו שלו מקבלו לחבירו, ששנינו "אם היתה עוברה זכתה לו" — אלמא שפחה זו מקבלתו לצורך עוברה מיד רבה:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:8:1.english: And if a person whispers to you - in your ear, to raise a difficulty and say: Behold, it is taught that even from the hand of his own master [a slave] can receive [a bill of manumission] for his fellow [slave], as we learned: "If she was pregnant, she acquires [freedom] for it [the fetus]" — thus, this maidservant receives it [the bill of manumission] on behalf of her fetus from the hand of her master:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:9:1.english: One who emancipates half of his slave acquires - the slave [acquires] that half:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:9:2.english: And one [of them] said - [He] adds to and completes the explanation of the matter:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:9:3.hebrew: מאי טעמא דרבי בהא - הא לא חצי עבדו הוא, דתרי גופי נינהו:
Rashi on Gittin 23b:9:3.english: What is Rabbi's reasoning for this - [After all,] this is not [a case of] half of his slave, for they are two [separate] bodies:

Rashi on Gittin 23b:9:4.english: He holds [that] a fetus is its mother's thigh - and it is like half of her body:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:14:1.hebrew: אדרבה איפכא מיסתברא - ורב יוסף סבר דמ"מ יכולה לקלקלה בחו"ל ע"י עדים וראיה שלא שלח לה הגט:
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:14:1.english: On the contrary, the opposite is reasonable - And Rav Yosef holds that nevertheless she can do her harm outside of Eretz Yisrael through witnesses and proof that [the husband] did not send her the bill of divorce:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:1:1.hebrew: אין העבד נעשה שליח כו' - וא"ת, ומתניתין ליתני עבד וכל שכן עובד כוכבים? וללישנא דאמר ר' יוחנן לעיל "זו אין תורה", ניחא דנקט עובד כוכבים למידק דלענין כתיבה אפילו עובד כוכבים כשר; אבל להך לישנא דמוקי ר' יוחנן כר"א, קשה מהך דר' יוחנן דהכא. ואור"ת דנקט עובד כוכבים לאשמועי' עובד כוכבים ונתגייר פסול, אע"פ שבאותה שעה היתה דעתו להתגייר, דהוי בעובד כוכבים רבותא טפי מבעבד שאין בידו להשתחרר:
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:1:1.english: A slave cannot become an agent, etc. - And if you will say: Let the Mishnah teach [the case of] a slave, and all the more so [would we know that] a gentile [is disqualified]? According to the version [in which] Rabbi Yoḥanan said earlier, "This is not the law," it is fine that [the Mishnah] chose [to teach the case of] a gentile, in order to infer that with respect to writing [a bill of divorce], even a gentile is fit. However, according to that version [in which] Rabbi Yoḥanan establishes [the Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, it is difficult from this [statement] of Rabbi Yoḥanan here! And Rabbeinu Tam says that [the Mishnah] chose [to teach the case of] a gentile to inform us [that if he was] a gentile and converted, he is disqualified, even though at that time his intention was to convert; for in [the case of] a gentile there is a greater novelty than in [the case of] a slave, who does not have it in his power to free himself:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:1:2.hebrew: לפי שאינו בתורת גיטין וקידושין - והא דמתגרשת בעבד שלה, היינו מטעם חצר:
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:1:2.english: Because he is not [included] in the laws of divorce and betrothal - And [the case] where she is divorced through her [own] slave is on account of [the law of] a courtyard:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:3:1.hebrew: העובד כוכבים והכותי שתרמו כו' - פי' בקונט' דקסבר אין קנין לעובד כוכבים. ונראה לר"י, דאפילו למ"ד יש קנין, משכחת לה כשגדלה שליש ביד ישראל וקנה ממנו עובד כוכבים, ולא מיפטר מטעם לוקח, ד"תבואת זרעך" קרינא ביה, כיון שגדלה הרבה ביד עובד כוכבים. אי נמי, כשזרעה העובד כוכבים ומכרה לישראל, וגדלה שליש, וחזר וקנאה ממנו. ועוד, דפי' ר"ת בספ"ק דבכורות (דף יא: ד"ה טבלים), דלא מיפטר לוקח היכא דלקח קודם שנתמרח. אי נמי, בחכר שדה מישראל, חייב הגדל בו בתרומה, ואפי' יש קנין לעובד כוכבי':
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:3:1.english: A gentile and a Samaritan who separated [teruma], etc. - Rashi explained that [the Tanna] holds a gentile has no [valid] acquisition [of land in the Land of Israel to exempt its produce from teruma]. But it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that even according to the one who says [a gentile] does have [valid] acquisition, you can find [this case] when it grew a third in the possession of a Jew and a gentile bought it from him; and he is not exempt on the grounds of being a purchaser, because we apply to it [the phrase] "the produce of your seed," since it grew significantly in the gentile's possession. Alternatively, [it is] when the gentile planted it, sold it to a Jew, it grew a third [in the Jew's possession], and [the gentile] went back and bought it from him. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam explained at the end of the first chapter of Bekhorot (11b, s.v. tevalim) that a purchaser is not exempt where he bought [the produce] before it was smoothed into a pile. Alternatively, where [a gentile] leased a field from a Jew, what grows in it is obligated in teruma, even if a gentile has [valid] acquisition [of land]:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:3:2.hebrew: תרומתו תרומה - והא דאמרי' בזבחים בפ' ב"ש (זבחים דף מה.) ופ"ק דתמורה (דף ב:), דקדשי עובדי כוכבים אין בהן משום מעילה, ומפרש טעמא משום דילפינן "חט" "חט" מתרומה, ובתרומה כתיב "בני ישראל" — אתיא כר' שמעון דפליג הכא בסיפא, ובריש פרק שני דקידושין (דף מא:) מייתי לה:
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:3:2.english: His teruma is teruma - And as for that which we say in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (Zevachim 45a) and [in] the first chapter of Temurah (2b), that consecrated offerings of gentiles are not subject to [the laws of] misappropriation of consecrated property, and [the Gemara] explains the reason [as being] because we derive [it via] "sin" [and] "sin" from teruma, and regarding teruma it is written "the children of Israel" — [that] follows Rabbi Shimon, who disagrees here in the latter clause, and at the beginning of the second chapter of Kiddushin (41b) [the Gemara] cites it:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:3:3.hebrew: ותנן עובד כוכבים שתרם את של ישראל כו' - הוה מצי לשנויי דאתיא כרבי שמעון, דסבר דליתא בתרומה דנפשיה בפרק שני דקדושין (דף מא:), אלא דעדיפא מיניה משני:
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:3:3.english: And we learned: An idolater who separated [terumah] from that of a Jew, etc. - [The Gemara] could have answered that [the latter Mishnah] follows Rabbi Shimon, who holds that [a gentile] is not included in [the law of] terumah for his own [produce], in the second chapter of Kiddushin (41b); rather, it gives a better answer than that:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:5:1.hebrew: מה אתם בני ברית - וא"ת: דבפ"ב דקידושין (גז"ש) משמע דלרבי שמעון לא איצטריך ליה למידרש "מה אתם בני ברית", ומוקי לה לדרשא אחריתי; וא"כ, לדידיה מנא לן הא דקי"ל בכל דוכתי דעובד כוכבים לאו בר שליחות הוא, לענין זכיה ורבית בפ' איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף עא:)? וי"ל, דמ"מ כיון דדרשי' שליחות מתרומה מ"גם אתם", ומינה ילפינן בעלמא, מסתמא דלא מרבינן בעלמא אלא דומיא ד"אתם":
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:5:1.english: Just as you are members of the covenant - And if you ask: In the second chapter of Kiddushin (gezeirah shavah), it implies that according to Rabbi Shimon, he does not need to expound "just as you are members of the covenant," and he establishes it for a different exposition; and if so, according to him, from where do we know that which we hold as established in all places, that a gentile is not capable of agency, regarding acquisition and interest in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 71b)? And one can say that nevertheless, since we derive agency from terumah, from "also you," and from it we learn [agency] in general, presumably we only include [agents] in general [when they are] similar to "you":

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:9:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דרבי גרסי' - ולא גרסי' דר' יוחנן, דבהערל (יבמות דף עח.) סבר ר' יוחנן דעובר לאו ירך אמו הוא, וכן מוכח סוגיא התם:
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:9:1.english: We read: "What is the reasoning of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]" - and we do not read "of Rabbi Yoḥanan," for in [the chapter entitled] He'arel (Yevamot 78a), Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that a fetus is not [considered] its mother's thigh, and so the passage there proves:

Tosafot on Gittin 23b:9:2.hebrew: ונעשה כמי שהקנה לה אחד מאבריה - תימה לר"י: היתה עוברה, היאך זכתה לו? אע"ג דירך אמו הוא, כיון דידה היא כיד רבה, שלא שיחרר אלא העובר — ואפילו שיחרר כולה חוץ מידה לא הוה לה לזכות לו; דכשמשחרר כולה, יש לה כח לזכות, משום דגיטה וידה באין כאחד, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא דקידושין (דף כג.):
Tosafot on Gittin 23b:9:2.english: And it is as though he transferred [ownership of] one of her limbs to her - This is astonishing to Ri: [in the case where] she was pregnant, how did she acquire [the writ of emancipation] for it? Even though [the fetus] is [considered] its mother's thigh, since her hand is like the hand of her master — for he only emancipated the fetus, and even if he had emancipated all of her except for her hand, she would not be able to acquire [it] for it! For [only] when he emancipates all of her does she have the power to acquire, because her document [of emancipation] and her hand [i.e., capacity to acquire] come simultaneously, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (23a):
